ratings_why.fun: Growing one vain giant on a deliberately empty board, fed by squires sold and names crossed out, is a clear and satisfying arc, and the three keywords now read cleanly.
ratings_why.distinct: Gaps as fuel and Proud chequerboards play unlike any tribe today; Duel itself is a familiar Start of Combat strike, which holds it at 7.

verdict_why: Two small wording holes remain (Dame Reisig against the Hen rule, and Konrad sold while he is the Champion); fix those and it should settle.

points.text: Dame Reisig says your Champion is your biggest unit of any tribe, but Champion says Hens are never Champion. Say whether a Hen, Reisig herself included, can be crowned under her.
If Squire Konrad is your biggest Knight he is the Champion, so selling him gives his stats to himself. Add 'another' or say the next Champion takes them.

The fantasy lands in the rules, not the names: dawn duels before the fight, standing alone as display, the shrinking order as fuel, hens who judge but are never crowned. Keep that voice in any revision.
Fantail Warden's Shield landing before or after the Champion's Duel depends on reading order; a short 'before Duels' would remove the puzzle for new players without losing the Shield.
Master of the Cork-Pop now reads well; showing the worked case on the card (Hartmut wins: two more Duels) would make the doubling instantly clear.

standouts.why: Sir Gottfried reads in one glance (x4 at six gaps) and is the whole tribe's fantasy in one card: the last knight, magnificent on an empty ridge.
The Chronicler crossing out a name each spring to feed the Champion is flavour turned directly into a rhythm of play.
Bilberry Hen judging winners, and judging Proud ones more, is simple text that braids two builds.

weakest.why: Pennon-Squire is a plain hand-out of a keyword with little woodland or lek flavour in what it does.
Grit-Pit Forager is a stone generator whose payoff is a generic stat item; the gizzard idea could do more.
Sprucehold Envoy is a standard Discover with a small-board rider; it works but says little about the order.

flags.note: Conflicts with the Champion keyword's rule that Hens are never Champion.
Sale effect has no target when Konrad is himself the Champion.
x4 (x7 golden) of a fed Champion in fight; the designer flags it as broken on purpose.
With Hartmut, Cork-Pop and Ottokar, pre-fight Duels may decide many fights before the first attack.
